newEntryDefaultBlocks.label: Starting blocks for a new page
newEntryDefaultBlocks.help: Comma-separated block type names, e.g. "prose". Pre-fills a new entry's blocks field instead of leaving it empty. Leave empty for no starting blocks.

homePath.label: Homepage
homePath.help: The path served at /, e.g. /home. Leave empty to keep the default (/home).

enabled.label: Allow comments
enabled.help: Site-wide default. A collection or an entry can still turn this off.

moderationRequired.label: Comments must be approved before showing

allowAnonymous.label: Allow comments from visitors without an account

notifyEmail.label: Notify this address of new comments
notifyEmail.help: Leave empty to disable e-mail notifications.

dataRetentionNote.label: Data retention note
dataRetentionNote.help: Shown to visitors, purely informational — nothing here changes what is actually retained.

priceDisplay.label: Price display
priceDisplay.help: Whether catalogue prices are shown tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive.

countriesServed.label: Countries served
countriesServed.help: Comma-separated two-letter codes, e.g. "FR, BE, LU". Leave empty to serve every country.

minOrderSubtotalMinor.label: Minimum order (minor units)
minOrderSubtotalMinor.help: 0 means no minimum. Amounts are in minor units — 500 is 5.00 in a two-decimal currency.

allowBackorderDefault.label: Allow selling past zero stock by default
allowBackorderDefault.help: A new variant's own setting can still override this.

tosPagePath.label: Terms of sale page
tosPagePath.help: A site-relative path to a real, published content entry, e.g. /terms.

returnPolicyPagePath.label: Return policy page
returnPolicyPagePath.help: A site-relative path to a real, published content entry, e.g. /returns.

invoiceSeriesPrefix.label: Invoice series prefix
invoiceSeriesPrefix.help: Prepended to the year-based series, e.g. "AC" + "2026" = series "AC2026". Letters, digits and hyphens only.

invoicePaymentTerms.label: Payment terms
invoicePaymentTerms.help: Printed on every invoice, e.g. "Payment due within 30 days."

invoiceLanguage.label: Invoice language
invoiceLanguage.help: A short language code, e.g. "en" or "fr".

showCogentaBranding.label: Show Cogenta branding
showCogentaBranding.help: Credits Cogenta in the public site's footer and in this admin's own header.

customLogoMediaId.label: Custom logo
customLogoMediaId.help: Shown instead of the Cogenta logo once branding is turned off above.

titleTemplate.label: General title template
titleTemplate.help: Applied to every page's derived title. Use %title% for the page's own title and %site% for the site name, e.g. "%title% — %site%". Leave empty for no template. Never applied to a page's own SEO title field.

defaultMetaDescription.label: Default meta description
defaultMetaDescription.help: Used only when a page has no description of its own.

twitterHandle.label: Twitter/X handle
twitterHandle.help: Used for the twitter:site tag, e.g. "@example".

defaultSocialImageUrl.label: Default social image
defaultSocialImageUrl.help: A path or an absolute URL, used as the Open Graph/Twitter Card image only when a page has none of its own.

enabled.label: Collect traces and logs locally
enabled.help: Powers this process's own recent-events buffer, shown below and in the Observability screen. Turning this off stops collection immediately, on every process.

logLevel.label: Log level captured
logLevel.help: How verbose the local log buffer is. Does not change what is written to this process's own stdout, only what shows up here.

autoUpdatePolicy.label: Automatic updates
autoUpdatePolicy.help: Off by default. When set, the site checks npm daily and applies any update that fits — never one whose changelog mentions a frozen contract, which is always left for manual review.

mcp.heading: MCP Server
mcp.adminOnly: Admin role only: this page creates and revokes MCP credentials.

mcp.nameHint: A label to recognise this key later, e.g. "Claude Desktop" or "my laptop".
mcp.scopeHint: One or more role names, separated by commas — the roles the connected MCP client is allowed to act as.
mcp.expiryHint: A key with no expiry is a key that leaks forever. 90 days is the recommended default.
mcp.expiryNeverWarning: This key will never expire on its own. Only choose this if you have a real reason to.

mcpClients.heading: MCP Clients
mcpClients.adminOnly: Admin role only: this page connects this site to external MCP servers.
mcpClients.intro: Connect this site's agents to an external MCP server — a stdio process this server spawns and talks to over the Model Context Protocol. Every remote tool is off by default: check exactly the ones an agent may call, one at a time.
mcpClients.newDescription: Only "stdio" connections are supported today — a command this server spawns and talks to over its standard input/output.
mcpClients.nameHint: A label to recognise this connection later.
mcpClients.commandHint: The executable to spawn, e.g. an absolute path. It receives no environment variables from this host unless listed below.
mcpClients.envHint: One NAME=value per line — exactly what the spawned process receives, nothing else, never this server's own environment.
mcpClients.authKindHint: How this connection authenticates itself to the remote server, if at all.
mcpClients.secretHint: Encrypted at rest. Never shown again once saved.
mcpClients.secretEnvVarHint: Which environment variable the decrypted secret is injected into when this connection is used.
mcpClients.unsandboxedWarningBody: A "stdio" connection spawns the command above with this Cogenta server's own full operating-system privileges — there is no worker/VM isolation for it, unlike a plugin. This screen's checkboxes only limit which of its tools an agent may call; they do not sandbox the process itself. Only connect a server you trust the way you would trust code you run directly on this machine.
mcpClients.unsandboxedConfirm: I understand this runs an unsandboxed executable with this server's own full privileges, and I trust it accordingly.

mcpClients.empty: No MCP connection has been created yet.
mcpClients.confirmRemove: Remove this connection? Every tool it exposes stops being available to every agent immediately.
mcpClients.manageToolsDescription: Only checked tools are ever offered to an agent — a tool discovered but never checked here does not exist for any agent, on this connection or any other.
mcpClients.noDiscoveredTools: This connection reported no tools the last time it was tested.

assistantIndex.heading: Knowledge index
assistantIndex.intro: The assistant answers questions and finds duplicates by searching an index built from two sources: your site's own published content, and any additional reference documents you upload here. Nothing that is only a draft is ever indexed.
assistantIndex.introShared: This index is shared: it is what powers both this admin assistant and, on a site that turns one on, a public assistant for visitors. There is no public assistant on this site yet — this is the same knowledge base it would draw from if one existed.
assistantIndex.loadError: Could not load the reference documents. Try again.
assistantIndex.toggleError: Could not save that change. Try again.
assistantIndex.uploadError: Could not upload that document. Try again.
assistantIndex.collectionsIntro: Every collection is indexed by default, using only its published entries — never a draft. Turn a collection off to leave it out of the index entirely, for example to keep published articles out of what the assistant can quote.
assistantIndex.collectionsEmpty: This site has no content collection to index.
assistantIndex.reindexHint: Turning a collection off removes it from new saves right away. Content indexed before the change stays until you run "Reindex vectors" from Tools & Health.
assistantIndex.adminOnlyEdit: Only an administrator can change which collections are indexed.
assistantIndex.documentsIntro: Upload a PDF, Word document, Markdown or plain-text file with information the assistant should know about but that is not part of your published content — a policy, a handbook, a specification. It is split into passages, turned into the same searchable form as your content, and can be cited in an answer just like a published entry.
assistantIndex.documentsEmpty: No reference document has been uploaded yet.

duplicates.intro: Compares one entry's text against this site's other content and reports near-identical matches. Nothing is merged or deleted automatically.

observability.heading: Observability
observability.intro: A local fallback view, not a replacement for a real APM: it shows only what this one server process has seen since it last started, bounded to the most recent entries. Point "Export destination" at Grafana, Datadog or any OTLP-speaking backend for real retention and alerting.

tools.heading: Tools
tools.intro: Maintenance tasks that would otherwise need a terminal. Every one of them runs in the background — this screen polls for progress rather than waiting on the request.
tools.checkExternalLinks: Also check external links (makes outbound requests)

scheduled.heading: Scheduled tasks
scheduled.modeInternal: Driven by the internal scheduler — this process ticks every task on its own.
scheduled.modeExternal: Driven by external cron — a scheduled command calls the tasks due; this process does not tick them on its own.
scheduled.contentBody: The list of entries waiting to publish is on the dashboard.
scheduled.confirmBody: This task is destructive — it permanently removes data. This cannot be undone.

content.summary: Cogenta's content: entries organised into collections (articles, pages…), classified by taxonomies, illustrated with media, and tracked over time by a version history. An entry moves through a simple editorial cycle — draft, optional review, publish — detailed below.

quickstart.step2: Create an entry: fill in its fields and lay it out with blocks.
quickstart.step3: Save it as a draft, then publish — right away or on a scheduled date.
quickstart.step4: Classify the entry with a taxonomy if the site declares one, and manage its images from the Media library.
quickstart.step5: A deleted entry goes to the Trash first, where it can be restored before it is permanently purged.

appearance.summary: The site's public appearance (colours, typography, logo, additional CSS), this admin's own theme, SEO (metadata, sitemap, robots.txt) and redirects.

quickstart.step1: Open “Appearance” to adjust colours and typography — the live preview shows the result before you save.
quickstart.step2: Drop a logo and favicon into “Identity”, or generate a theme with AI if a provider is configured.
quickstart.step3: Check a page's SEO under “SEO”: title, meta description, sitemap.
quickstart.step4: Add a redirect under “Redirects” whenever a URL moves.

commerce.summary: The shop: products and variants, orders, coupons, subscriptions, and the store's financial setup (tax, shipping, payment methods).

quickstart.step1: Add a first product under “Products” to make the Commerce group appear in the sidebar.
quickstart.step2: Set up tax, shipping and a payment method under the store settings before the first sale.
quickstart.step3: Track incoming orders under “Orders” — every status change is logged.
quickstart.step4: Create a discount coupon if needed, or a subscription for a recurring product.
quickstart.step5: A content entry can be linked to a product record to keep rich text, blocks and SEO from the content contract.

ai.summary: The AI assistant (writing help, translation, duplicate detection…), the site's autonomous agents, and AI-driven site creation from an uploaded document. None of it is required for the CMS to work: with no provider configured, this section explains where to plug one in rather than staying silent.

quickstart.step1: Open “Assistant”: with no provider configured, the screen explains how to add one.
quickstart.step2: Once configured, use the assist tools directly from an entry's editor (rewrite, translate, summarise…).
quickstart.step3: Check “Agents” to see an agent's full declared configuration.
quickstart.step4: Use “Create a site” to propose a content model and templates from a document — every proposal waits for explicit approval, never an automatic apply.

accounts.summary: This admin's human and machine accounts: users and their roles, API keys for headless access, and the permission matrix by role.

quickstart.step1: Invite a user under “Users” and assign them a role.
quickstart.step2: Check “Roles & permissions” to see, action by action, what a role can do.
quickstart.step3: Create an API key under “API keys” for a headless client — it carries its own permissions, independent of any human account.
quickstart.step4: Revoke or rotate a compromised key from the same screen, at any time.

settings.summary: The site's general settings (title, time zone, home page, comments, media, privacy) and your own profile. Infrastructure configuration (security, webhooks) stays read-only here — it comes from cogenta.config.mjs.

quickstart.step1: Open “Settings” for the site title, time zone and home page.
quickstart.step2: Choose whether comments are allowed by default, and whether a cookie banner is needed.
quickstart.step3: Check “Security & webhooks” (read-only) to see what cogenta.config.mjs actually configured.
quickstart.step4: Update your own profile (password, preferences) under “My profile”.

editorial.heading: Editorial cycle: from draft to published
editorial.intro: What happens to an entry from the moment it is created until it is visible on the site — with or without a review step.

steps.step1: A newly created entry is a draft: nothing is visible on the site.
steps.step2: If the collection has review turned on, submitting the entry moves it to “submitted” — it waits for a reviewer.
steps.step3: The reviewer approves it, or requests changes; a change request goes back to “submitted” once fixed.
steps.step4: Publishing is a separate action from approval — approving never publishes automatically.
steps.step5: An entry can also be scheduled: it stays a draft until the chosen date, then publishes itself.

editorial.note: Review is optional, collection by collection — a collection that has not turned it on goes straight from draft to published.

plugin.heading: A third-party plugin's permissions: from install to revocation
plugin.intro: What a Marketplace plugin can actually do, and how that access is closed off again.

steps.step1: The plugin declares in its manifest the capabilities it asks for, from a closed vocabulary (read content, call the web, write to storage…).
steps.step2: Before installation, those capabilities are shown in plain language for review.
steps.step3: Once installed, only the intersection of what the manifest asks for and what was actually granted reaches the plugin's code — never the requested list as-is.
steps.step4: If the plugin exceeds its time or memory limits, or crashes, it is disabled automatically; resuming it needs a human action.
steps.step5: Deactivating or uninstalling the plugin closes off its access; uninstalling with data removal revokes every one of its permissions at once.

plugin.note: An honest model, not yet fully on screen: revoking a single capability after the fact has the logic for it server-side, but no screen in this build exposes it yet — today, deactivating or uninstalling is the lever available.
